topic_and_scope: This pilot cross-sectional study compares long-term traditional cigarette smokers (SMs) with non-smokers (non-SMs) to evaluate retinal microvascular changes via OCTA, systemic thrombus formation via T-TAS, and pulmonary function via spirometry. The work aims to identify OCTA parameters correlated with smoking-related retinal damage and to explore associations with systemic vascular and respiratory function, noting limitations such as small sample size and exposure scope.
main_themes: Smoking-associated retinal microvascular changes detectable by OCTA, with macular flow density (FD) reduction observed in smokers.
Altered systemic hemostasis in smokers demonstrated by T-TAS indicators of accelerated thrombus formation.
Concurrent pulmonary function impairment alongside ocular and hematologic changes, with indications for broader, longitudinal investigations and AMD-related considerations.
main_findings: Macular flow density (FD) was significantly reduced in smokers versus non-smokers, while other OCTA parameters (superficial/deep vessel density, FAZ, Ch-Flow) showed no significant differences in this small cohort.

Smokers exhibited signs of accelerated primary hemostasis (significantly lower OT and significantly higher AUC on T-TAS) and had a significantly reduced FEV1, with other spirometric indices not reaching statistical significance; these findings point to combined ocular microvascular and systemic vascular alterations associated with chronic smoking.

key_gaps.description: Small, single-center sample with limited demographic balance and exposure scope (only traditional cigarettes), restricting generalizability of OCTA and T-TAS findings.

Lack of longitudinal data to establish causality, reversibility after cessation, and temporal evolution of OCTA, T-TAS, and spirometric changes; AMD status and exposure type (e-cigarettes, other products) are not addressed.

future_directions.title: Expand cohort size and diversify exposure types across multiple centers
future_directions.rationale: The current study is limited by a small, single-center sample of traditional cigarette smokers. A larger, multicenter design with balanced gender representation and broader age ranges, including non-traditional tobacco products and e-cigarettes, will improve statistical power, enable subgroup analyses (gender, age, comorbidities), and test the generalizability of OCTA and T-TAS differences across populations. Implement standardized OCTA and T-TAS protocols, preregister analyses, and ensure consistent data collection across sites.

future_directions.title: Longitudinal follow-up of smokers undergoing cessation to assess reversibility
future_directions.rationale: To determine whether smoking-related ocular, hematologic, and pulmonary changes are reversible, implement a longitudinal study with follow-ups at 6, 12, and 24 months post-cessation. Measure OCTA metrics (FD, SVD, DVD, FAZ, Ch-Flow), T-TAS parameters (OT, AUC), and spirometric indices, and correlate trajectories with duration since cessation and relapse risk. This will inform whether cessation yields recovery of microvascular and thrombotic function and the time course of any changes.

future_directions.title: Incorporate AMD status and smoker subgroups with distinct retinal pathologies
future_directions.rationale: Given the proposed link between smoking and AMD, recruit smokers with colloid, atrophic, or exudative AMD and compare to non-smokers without AMD to determine whether smoking amplifies retinal vascular alterations in AMD and whether OCTA metrics predict AMD progression in smokers. This could establish smoking status as a modifier of AMD-related vascular changes and guide targeted monitoring.

future_directions.title: Include electronic nicotine delivery systems and other tobacco products
future_directions.rationale: Expand exposure groups to include e-cigarettes and non-tobacco products to differentiate retinal microvascular and thrombotic effects by modality and dose. This will clarify whether observed OCTA and T-TAS alterations are driven by nicotine exposure, combustion-related toxins, or other product-specific constituents, enabling more precise public health guidance.

future_directions.title: Expand biomarker panels to probe mechanisms linking smoking to vascular changes
future_directions.rationale: Add systemic biomarkers of oxidative stress (e.g., GSH/GSSG, MDA), NO bioavailability, inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6), MMPs, and coagulation factors (fibrinogen, D-dimer). Correlate these with T-TAS and OCTA metrics to elucidate the biological pathways driving smoking-related ocular and systemic vascular alterations, informing targeted interventions.

future_directions.title: Dose-response analyses to identify exposure thresholds
future_directions.rationale: Model relationships between pack-years, cigarettes-per-day, and duration with OCTA (FD, Ch-Flow), T-TAS (OT, AUC), and spirometric outcomes to identify exposure thresholds associated with detectable vascular damage. This can guide risk stratification and public health messaging regarding safe exposure limits, if any.

future_directions.title: Standardize and validate OCTA-derived biomarkers across devices and protocols
future_directions.rationale: To ensure robustness and reproducibility of FD and other OCTA parameters as biomarkers of smoking-related retinal damage, perform cross-device validation, inter-operator reliability studies, and protocol harmonization. This will enable cross-study comparisons and facilitate clinical translation of OCTA metrics as monitoring tools in smoking-related vascular disease.
